sweepNotes: Reviewed QuantConnect/Lean as a maintained event-driven trading architecture and compared its patterns with TAGX premarket reliability. No production dependency added. Adopted only the provider-fallback and deterministic state-management patterns into TAGX's native Python heartbeat.

candidates.purpose: Reference architecture for event-driven ingestion, broker/data adapters, backtesting/live parity, fallback data providers, risk controls and deterministic engine state.
candidates.latencySuitability: HIGH as an engine pattern; direct integration is too heavy for TAGX GitHub-Actions architecture
candidates.maintenance: Very active; multiple merged commits on 2026-08-26, including brokerage integration, indicator reset contracts and live-data fallback handling.
candidates.docsTests: README describes an event-driven modular trading platform with live trading and backtesting; repository CI includes build/regression tests and recent commits add explicit test coverage.
candidates.securityNotes: Direct engine/broker integration would materially expand attack surface and secret-management requirements. Keep brokerage credentials server-side and out of GitHub Pages.
candidates.lookAheadBiasRisk: LOW when its event-time/live-backtest parity patterns are followed; MEDIUM if TAGX imports historical state without preserving observation timestamps.
candidates.integrationPlan: Borrow provider fallback, event-time state and reset-contract patterns. Do not install LEAN. Benchmark any future standalone replay adapter in a challenger branch first.
